label: UniProtKB accession
authority: Checked for G1 on 2026-10-29 against UniProt's help. Accessions: 'UniProtKB accession numbers consist of 6 or 10 alphanumerical characters', matching [OPQ][0-9][A-Z0-9]{3}[0-9]|[A-NR-Z][0-9]([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2}[0-9]){1,2} (https://www.uniprot.org/help/accession_numbers, last modified 2026-06-12). The format has upper-case letters only, so the case policy is upper: p04637 is P04637. Accessions are cited without a version, so none is split off. One accession space for every organism: scope global. Isoforms: 'a unique identifier, which is composed of the primary accession number of the entry, followed by a dash and a number' (https://www.uniprot.org/help/alternative_products). An entry accession defines a protein and an accession with any isoform suffix, -1 included, defines a protein_isoform; the two are never collapsed, because the canonical sequence is chosen 'for display' (https://www.uniprot.org/help/canonical_and_isoforms). An isoform number is written without leading zeros, and P04637-01 is rejected rather than rewritten. Merged and split entries keep old accessions as secondary accessions, which are not unique.

label: HGNC ID
authority: Checked for G1 on 2026-10-29: 'A unique ID provided by the HGNC for each gene with an approved symbol. IDs are of the format HGNC:n, where n is a unique number. HGNC IDs remain stable even if a name or symbol changes.' (https://www.genenames.org/help/symbol-report/). Human genes only, so fixed to taxon 9606, where it defines gene identity (owner's decision, 2026-10-29). Normalization, settled in G1's review: the lookup is HGNC:<n> with no leading zeros (HGNC:05 is HGNC:5); the HGNC: prefix is accepted in any case; a bare number is accepted only when the hgnc namespace is named, never when a term is resolved without a namespace, because a bare number could be an NCBI Gene ID. HGNC's REST service returns IDs in this form (https://rest.genenames.org/fetch/hgnc_id/11998 gives HGNC:11998, TP53).

label: NCBI Gene ID
authority: Checked for G1 on 2026-10-29: 'GeneID: the unique identifier for a gene' (NCBI Gene README, https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/README, last modified January 2, 2025), with the organism in a separate tax_id column, so one ID space for every organism: scope global. GeneIDs are integers (identifiers.org ncbigene, pattern ^\d+$, https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ncbigene), written without leading zeros; other forms are rejected. Digits have no case. Discontinued GeneIDs are listed in gene_history. Cross-reference only (owner's decision, 2026-10-29): a GeneID never creates a gene, and maps to one only through a cross-reference that an approved release states.

label: Ensembl gene ID
authority: Checked for G1 on 2026-10-29: 'Stable IDs are created in the form ENS[species prefix][feature type prefix][a unique eleven digit number]', the feature type prefix of a gene being G (https://www.ensembl.org/info/genome/stable_ids/index.html and prefixes.html, read from their source in the Ensembl/public-plugins repository, branch release/116). Human genes have no species prefix (ENSG00000141510, TP53) and mouse genes have MUS (ENSMUSG00000059552, Trp53), so IDs never collide across species: scope global. A gene's version increments 'when the set of transcripts linked to a gene changes' and is written after a dot (ENSG00000141510.21; identifiers.org ensembl pattern, https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ensembl); it is split off and kept, and the lookup is the unversioned ID. Upper case by definition. Cross-reference only (owner's decision, 2026-10-29): an Ensembl gene ID never creates a gene, and maps to one only through a cross-reference that an approved release states.

label: Synthetic gene ID
authority: Defined by openPIP for synthetic demonstration data only: no external authority, and no value names a real gene. Fixed to NCBI taxon 32630, 'synthetic construct' (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=32630). A value is SYN-, an upper-case letter, then upper-case letters and digits, kept exactly as written. Genes only: synthetic proteins have their own namespace, because one namespace never identifies both genes and proteins.

label: Synthetic protein ID
authority: Defined by openPIP for synthetic demonstration data only: no external authority, and no value names a real protein. Fixed to NCBI taxon 32630, 'synthetic construct' (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?id=32630). A value is SYN-, an upper-case letter, then upper-case letters and digits, kept exactly as written. As in UniProtKB, a value with a -<number> suffix, -1 included, defines a protein_isoform and one without defines a protein.
